source: compiled from the library's own texts

1.1:
*In the New Testament, outside the Gospels*
“It is more blessed to give than to receive.”
— Paul, quoting the Lord (`!verse Acts 20:35`)

2.1:
*In the Apostolic Fathers*
“Though ye be gathered together with Me in My bosom, and do not My commandments, I will cast you away and will say unto you, Depart from Me, I know you not whence ye are, ye workers of iniquity.”
— 2 Clement 4:5 (`!verse 2 Clement 4:5`)
2.2:
“Let not the lambs fear the wolves after they are dead; and ye also, fear ye not them that kill you and are not able to do anything to you; but fear Him that after ye are dead hath power over soul and body, to cast them into the Gehenna of fire.”
— 2 Clement 5:2-4 (`!verse 2 Clement 5:4`)
2.3:
“When the two shall be one, and the outside as the inside, and the male with the female, neither male or female.”
— 2 Clement 12:2 (`!verse 2 Clement 12:2`)
2.4:
“Behold I make the last things as the first.”
— The Epistle of Barnabas 6:13 (`!verse Epistle of Barnabas 6:13`)
2.5:
“They that desire to see Me, and to attain unto My kingdom, must lay hold on Me through tribulation and affliction.”
— The Epistle of Barnabas 7:11 (`!verse Epistle of Barnabas 7:11`)
2.6:
“Lay hold and handle me, and see that I am not a demon without body.”
— Ignatius, To the Smyrnaeans 3:2 (`!verse Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 3:2`)

3.1:
*In the Church Fathers*
“The days will come in which vines shall grow, having each ten thousand branches, and in each branch ten thousand twigs, and in each true twig ten thousand shoots, and in every one of the shoots ten thousand clusters, and on every one of the clusters ten thousand grapes, and every grape when pressed will give five-and-twenty metretes of wine.”
— Papias, as Irenaeus reports him (`!verse Fragments (Papias) 3:1`)
3.2:
“In whatsoever things I shall take you, in these I shall judge you.”
— Justin Martyr, Dialogue with Trypho 47 (`!verse Dialogue with Trypho 47:4`)
3.3:
“Be skilful money-changers rejecting some things, but retaining what is good.”
— Clement of Alexandria, Stromateis 1.28 (`!verse Stromateis 1.28:1`)
3.4:
“Be ye good money-changers”
— The Clementine Homilies, Homily 2 (`!verse Clementine Homilies 2:52`)
3.5:
“My mystery is to me, and to the sons of my house”
— Clement of Alexandria, Stromateis 5.10 (`!verse Stromateis 5.10:2`)
3.6:
“Ask for the great things and the little shall be added unto you” and “Ask for the heavenly things and the earthly shall be added unto you”
— Origen, On Prayer (`!verse On Prayer 1:6`)
3.7:
“Because of the weak I was weak, and I hungered because of the hungry, and I thirsted because of the thirsty”
— Origen, Commentary on Matthew 13.2 (`!verse Commentary on the Gospel of Matthew 13.2:1`)
3.8:
“Good things must needs come, and blessed, said he, is he by whom they come; in like manner evil things must needs come, but woe to him through whom they come.”
— The Clementine Homilies 12.29 (`!verse Clementine Homilies 12:29`)

4.1:
*From the Gospel of the Hebrews, as the Fathers quote it*
“He that wonders shall reign, and he that has reigned shall rest.”
— Clement of Alexandria, Stromateis 2.9 (`!verse Stromateis 2.9:4`)
4.2:
“My mother, the Holy Spirit took me just now by one of my hairs and carried me off to the great mount Tabor”
— Origen, Commentary on John 2.6 (`!verse Commentary on the Gospel of John 2.6:1`)
4.3:
“My brother eat thy bread, for the son of man is risen from among those that sleep.”
— Jerome, Lives of Illustrious Men 2 (`!verse Lives of Illustrious Men 2:2`)

5.1:
*In Islamic tradition*
“The world is a bridge, so pass over it and do not inhabit it.”
— Robson, Christ in Islam (1929) (`!verse Christ in Islam 4:21`)
